Markus / team — draft position below and attached text file with the exact language to propose back to Orchid. Kept it intentionally pragmatic so sales can move quickly with the customer. Key points:

- Scope: Redwood will indemnify and defend only for third-party claims alleging infringement arising from Redwood's proprietary model weights or customer-specific modifications to Redwood-delivered models (not general model outputs trained on public data). We exclude claims based solely on user prompts or customer-provided data.
- Control & cooperation: Redwood requests the right to assume defense with counsel of its choice; Orchid can participate at its own expense. Redwood will not settle admissions of liability without Orchid's consent when Orchid is a named party.
- Cap & insurance: Monetary liability limited to the greater of (i) direct damages up to 3x annual contract value (ACV) or (ii) Redwood's applicable insurance proceeds covering the claim.
- Evidence & mitigation: Claim triggers require written notice, reasonable substantiation (complaint, claim letter), and a 60-day mitigation/review period during which parties will attempt to remediate or replace accused materials.
- Carveouts: Standard carveouts for infringement arising from (a) Orchid modifications to delivered models, (b) combination with third-party tech not supplied by Redwood, and (c) open-source dependencies per their OSS licenses.

Suggested short language to send (attached as proposed-indemnity-text-AO342.txt). I've flagged two negotiables: cap multiplier (we used 3x ACV as middle ground) and the 60-day remediation window. If Orchid pushes for uncapped, propose insurer-first approach and exclude punitive/indirect damages explicitly.

Let me know if you want me to send this directly or if sales will do the outreach. If you prefer I go direct to Evan, confirm and I'll copy the proposed redline into the Word doc track changes.

Evan — thanks for the redlines and for the patience while we looped in legal. Attached is a short note + tracked language proposing a middle path we think preserves your protection while keeping liability manageable for Redwood. High level: Redwood will provide an indemnity for qualifying third-party infringement claims tied to Redwood-delivered model weights or proprietary components, with a monetary cap tied to 3x ACV or available insurance proceeds (whichever is lower). We also propose a 60-day mitigation window so engineering teams can evaluate/replace any accused artifacts prior to triggering settlement obligations.

We believe this approach is in the spirit of what you asked for and protects both sides — it keeps indemnity focused on code/model IP rather than the broader and hard-to-control space of generated outputs.

Next steps: please review the attached tracked Word doc. If Orchid is comfortable in principle, can we get a short call Tuesday morning (PT) to lock final wording before your procurement review? If not, please mark your preferred changes and we'll iterate quickly.
